question_1: Does this piece carry one idea as clearly as The Ladder (Mon 2 Nov): one object, every move meaning something, nothing acting out a sentence? (.claude/agents/ve-critic.md, "First, beside his favourite")
question_2: Is any number on screen invented: a figure the piece does not own (its datasets, real artifacts or his script)? The spec's own never-list is the rule.

style_idea.object: the auditor going through the past: every old page it opens turns up either money (cash down the back of the sofa) or a skeleton (out of the cupboard)

moves.move: a real page or number slams onto the stage on the word that names it
moves.means: the past is written down, so it can be checked

moves.move: the big number is struck through and counts down
moves.means: what the audit found, in the family's own account

moves.move: cash comes out of the sofa
moves.means: the missing money an audit finds

moves.move: a skeleton tumbles out of the cupboard
moves.means: what else it finds, and it does not care whose cupboard it is

never: a re-typed headline standing in for the real page
a generated picture standing in for a real record
a joke aimed at the family, the viewer or a named person
invented numbers: every figure on screen is either the family's account as Tom's Hardware reported it or a figure printed on a named real page shown as itself

real_artifacts.text: Grieving family uses AI chatbot to cut hospital bill from $195,000 to $33,000

storyboard.point: AI just cut a family's six-figure hospital bill to a fraction
Imagine what it is finding in everyone's old paperwork, when whole hospital teams missed it
Will your AI auditor find the missing money?
Or will it find the skeletons in your closet?
A real family owed the whole bill after a death with no health cover
He asked for the bill line by line and gave it to Claude
Care was billed under a dearer code than the care he got
Charged for a steak, served a sandwich
He sent the list and the bill fell to about a sixth
An old bill can't argue back, the rules are written down, and AI reads every line without a break
About next year AI is guessing; about last year it is reading
Whose mistake did Claude find? The hospital's
It didn't care whose closet it was opening
And it won't care when it opens yours
This week he hands his own AI last year's invoices, to find his skeletons first
The full story is free at makeyourmindup.ai

pre_show_checklist.text: A graphic and a photo never both carry the same point: one picture per beat.
pre_show_checklist.krish: two concurrent visual styles trying to say the same thing over one another? why?

pre_show_checklist.text: A graphics beat sits on a graded, focus-racked backdrop, never flat black after a photograph; figures are never dimmed or blurred.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Motion graphics on a flat black background, straight after a full-frame photograph.

pre_show_checklist.text: A change between a full-screen beat and a face beat is a clean cut; never a cross-dissolve over his face.
pre_show_checklist.krish: A ghost of his face in dissolves.

pre_show_checklist.text: The wordmark appears only on the title frame and the closing card: no icons or company logos anywhere else unless he asks.
pre_show_checklist.krish: NO ICONS, ONLY THE WORDMARK DURING THE TITLE FRAME AND THE CLOSING FRAME

pre_show_checklist.text: off.day is never drawn as a pill, header or label, in any cut.
pre_show_checklist.krish: off.day is NEVER to be used ever as a tag

pre_show_checklist.text: Captions stay off for the whole title moment: check every frame of the title hold for caption text.
pre_show_checklist.krish: A stray caption word (find) under the held episode title

pre_show_checklist.text: On face beats captions sit in the staged band below his face; no caption page over his face.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Captions over his head.

pre_show_checklist.text: The episode title is built from his spoken line, timed to his words, at full stage width, as a card that slams or slides in over his hair, never bare words over his face.
pre_show_checklist.krish: make the title captions a card that slams or slides in I think. having naked captions over my face looks stupid.

pre_show_checklist.text: The title is one full-frame lockup, centred, type filling the frame, the wordmark inside it and on screen only while the title is; the title frame was looked at at full size.
pre_show_checklist.krish: I expect the title card to enter as I am talking, and the title of the piece is woven in to my script at the start. This is a good example of what actually was a good build for the title card.

pre_show_checklist.text: The figure a beat exists to show fills the frame.
pre_show_checklist.krish: The key figure (41) was too small.

pre_show_checklist.text: The bed sits 15% under the house level and is ridden by EBU R128 loudness, never RMS; the bed level does not swing.
pre_show_checklist.krish: The music was too loud, and the bed level swung.

pre_show_checklist.text: A track in config/music-library.json that he approved plays with no certificate check blocking it.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Aspire is "100% licensed"

pre_show_checklist.text: Every restart and dead silence is cut where a quiet gap allows; any kept is named with its timestamp.
pre_show_checklist.krish: A false start left in his take.

pre_show_checklist.text: Something lands on his first word (a line slamming in, a clip in motion, a punch-in); the joke or twist is visible before 3 seconds; never a static card that waits.
pre_show_checklist.krish: considering that's the first few seconds of the video, it's not much of a hook. It looks quite dull for the first 3 seconds.

pre_show_checklist.text: His whole head is in frame on his lines; no split frame crops his head or ruins the picture above it.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Can't cut my head off and also ruin the visual above.

pre_show_checklist.text: On every 16:9 proof beat his take sits in the bottom-right window, opposite the left-set captions, unless a full-frame clip fills the frame.
pre_show_checklist.krish: my head needs to be in the bottom right ... if the subtitles are going to be not centralised, then something needs to be in the bottom right.

pre_show_checklist.text: Words over a busy picture or his take get the approved halo; a page never breaks mid-phrase and the web address stays on one caption.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Approve halo

pre_show_checklist.text: The piece is funny and tongue-in-cheek; plates, devices and art direction come from Codex cards; every visual makes a point land faster.
pre_show_checklist.krish: This piece needs to be hilarious and tongue-in-cheek ... use codex for all asset production, generation, sourcing.

pre_show_checklist.text: Every known fault is fixed before he sees the file; none is listed as a caveat.
pre_show_checklist.krish: If you know that things need fixing, just fucking fix them

pre_show_checklist.text: Fixes are batched and checked here; the cut is shown to him once, not once per round.
pre_show_checklist.krish: Each round of fixes went to him as a new render instead of being checked first

pre_show_checklist.text: When he asks for a route the engine does not have, say so in one line with the closest real route before doing anything.
pre_show_checklist.krish: render in Codex

pre_show_checklist.text: Every beat serves the idea he picked (style.idea.object); a request for more ("15/10") is answered with more of that idea, never spectacle beside it.
pre_show_checklist.krish: (as the Build or buy session reported his words) a dull, important topic needs 15/10 visuals

pre_show_checklist.text: No long stretch of his face with nothing on screen, and no logos that only appear and pulse standing in for a picture (ve lint piece.talking_head).
pre_show_checklist.krish: (as the Build or buy session reported his words) a dull, important topic needs 15/10 visuals
